mainTopic: Mentioning and asking for rain, the miracle year of יואל, and רב נחמן's questions to רבי יצחק on puzzling פסוקים.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about mentioning rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם) in תפילה. רבא and רב ששת say that once you start mentioning rain, you do not stop. Even רב changed his mind to agree, and the הלכה follows this view. A new משנה then asks until when we ask for rain. רבי יהודה says until פסח has passed, and רבי מאיר says until ניסן ends, based on a פסוק in יואל. רב נחמן asks how that פסוק can put the first rain (יורה) in ניסן when it normally falls in מרחשון. רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן that the פסוק describes a famine year in the days of יואל, when the first rain came on ראש חודש ניסן and the grain grew miraculously in eleven days. The גמרא then brings a series of other puzzling פסוקים that רב נחמן asked רבי יצחק about: a seven-year famine, the heavenly and earthly ירושלים, and the one sin of עבודה זרה. The last question, about the 'two evils' in ירמיה, begins here, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא: once you start mentioning rain, you don't stop
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different view: once a person begins mentioning rain in תפילה, he keeps mentioning it and does not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Once he has started, he does not stop again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with the earlier view that one mentions rain and then stops. He rules that once you begin mentioning rain, you keep going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view said that outside ארץ ישראל, where the date of the holiday is in doubt, one mentions rain on the first day and then stops. רבא says the doubt does not matter: a person who has begun should not flip back and forth. From the start of mentioning rain, it continues through the whole rainy season.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Once he has started (to mention rain),
phrases.notes: Refers to mentioning rain (מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ וּמוֹרִיד הַגֶּשֶׁם) in the מוסף of שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: he does not stop again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל, שׁוּב אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from the view (on the previous עמוד) that one mentions rain and then stops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once one begins mentioning rain in תפילה, one continues and does not stop.

steps.title: רב ששת says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת independently holds the same rule as רבא: once you start, you don't stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said the same: Once he has started, he does not stop again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second אמורא, רב ששת, who holds exactly like רבא. This strengthens רבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule itself. The point is that a second major authority agrees, so רבא's position is not a lone opinion.

phrases.english: And so too Rav Sheshet said:
Once he has started, he does not stop again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second authority who agrees with רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת also rules that once one starts mentioning rain, one does not stop.

steps.title: Even רב changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב, who held the earlier view, later retracted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רב retracted (his earlier view).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that רב himself changed his mind and now agrees that one does not stop. This is a setup line, and the next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was a source of the earlier opinion that one mentions rain and then stops. If רב retracted, the main opposing voice is gone, which prepares the ground for the final ruling.

phrases.english: And even Rav retracted his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַב הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the authority behind the opposing view now agrees with רבא and רב ששת.

steps.title: Proof of רב's retraction: count 21 days, then start and never stop
steps.stepSummary: רב חננאל quotes רב: count 21 days from ראש השנה, as one counts ten days to יום כיפור. Then one begins mentioning rain and does not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חננאל said in the name of רב: One counts twenty-one days, the same way one counts ten days from ראש השנה until יום הכיפורים. Then he begins, and once he has begun, he does not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רב retracted by quoting a later statement of his. In it, רב says outright that once you start, you don't stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives a simple counting method. Count 21 days from ראש השנה, and the next day, שמיני עצרת, you begin mentioning rain. The key words are 'once he has started, he does not stop,' the very rule of רבא and רב ששת, so רב clearly changed his mind.
steps.confusionAlert: Counting 21 days does not mean you start on day 21. You count 21 days from ראש השנה and then begin, which brings you to שמיני עצרת, the 22nd of תשרי.

phrases.english: As Rav Chananel said that Rav said:
One counts twenty-one days
in the same way that one counts ten days
from Rosh HaShanah until Yom Kippur,
and (then) he begins (to mention rain),
and once he has begun, he does not stop again.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence for the claim that רב retracted.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רב retracted his earlier view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חננאל quoting רב: count 21 days, begin, and once begun do not stop.

steps.title: Final ruling: once you start, you don't stop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows the view that once one begins mentioning rain, one does not stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: Once he has started, he does not stop again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling and closes this discussion about mentioning rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבא, רב ששת, and even רב agreeing, the הלכה is settled. Even outside ארץ ישראל, where the date of the holiday is in doubt, one begins on שמיני עצרת and keeps mentioning rain.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: once you begin saying משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם, you keep saying it and do not stop, even in חוץ לארץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practice today. We begin mentioning rain in מוסף of שמיני עצרת and continue straight through the winter.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
Once he has started, he does not stop again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל, שׁוּב אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the agreement of all the authorities into a binding ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that once one starts mentioning rain, one does not stop.

steps.title: משנה: until when do we ask for rain?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks until when we ask for rain. רבי יהודה says until פסח passes. רבי מאיר says until ניסן ends, based on a פסוק in יואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Until when do we ask for rain? רבי יהודה says: Until פסח has passed. רבי מאיר says: Until ניסן has ended, as it says: 'And He brought down rain for you, the first rain and the last rain, in the first (month).'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: when we stop asking for rain. Two תנאים give different end points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ends at פסח, since rain after that is not helpful. רבי מאיר extends it through all of ניסן because the פסוק says rain fell 'in the first month,' meaning ניסן. That shows ניסן still counts as a rainy month.

keyTerms.meaning: we ask for rain (ותן טל ומטר)
the last rain of the season

steps.confusionAlert: Asking for rain (שאלה, ותן טל ומטר) is different from mentioning rain (הזכרה, משיב הרוח). The earlier steps were about mentioning, and this משנה is about asking.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Until when do we ask for rain?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר הַפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until Pesach has passed;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא נִיסָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Until Nisan has ended,
as it is stated: 'And He brought down rain for you,'
the first rain and the last rain, in the first (month).'

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד מָתַי שׁוֹאֲלִין אֶת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about when asking for rain ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: רבי יהודה says ask until פסח passes; רבי מאיר says until the end of ניסן, based on the פסוק in יואל.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks: the first rain is in מרחשון, not ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רבי מאיר's פסוק. The יורה falls in מרחשון, as a ברייתא teaches, so how can the פסוק put it in ניסן?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: The first rain in ניסן? The first rain is in מרחשון! As we learned: The first rain is in מרחשון and the last rain is in ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question on the פסוק quoted in the משנה. Read simply, the פסוק says the first rain fell in ניסן, but that contradicts a known ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the יורה, the first rain, comes at the start of winter in מרחשון, and only the מלקוש comes in ניסן. Yet the פסוק lists both יורה and מלקוש 'in the first month.' רב נחמן asks how the יורה could be in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmudic discussion on the משנה
the first rain of the season
as we learned (in a תנאי source)

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak:
The first rain in Nisan?
The first rain is in Marcheshvan!
As we learned:
The first rain is in Marcheshvan and the last rain is in Nisan!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק: יוֹרֶה בְּנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of the פסוק that רבי מאיר quoted in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק 'יורה ומלקוש בראשון,' which seems to place the first rain in ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the יורה is in מרחשון and only the מלקוש is in ניסן, so the פסוק seems to contradict the known order of the rains.

steps.title: Answer: in יואל's days, the first rain only came on ראש חודש ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן. The פסוק describes a special year in the days of יואל בן פתואל, when no rain fell all winter and the first rain came on the first of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוחנן said as follows: This verse was fulfilled in the days of יואל בן פתואל, about whom it is written: 'What the גזם left, the ארבה ate…'. That year אדר ended and no rain had fallen; the first rainfall came down for them on the first of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers רב נחמן's question by quoting רבי יוחנן. The פסוק does not describe a normal year, only one unusual year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the יורה comes in מרחשון. But in יואל's time there was a terrible famine with plagues of locusts, and no rain fell all winter until אדר ended. That year the first rain came on ראש חודש ניסן, so the פסוק could truly say 'the first rain… in the first month.'

keyTerms.meaning: what the גזם (locust type) left, the ארבה (locust) ate
the first rainfall of the season
the month of אדר, before ניסן

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's order is the normal rule: יורה in מרחשון, מלקוש in ניסן. The פסוק in יואל describes one unusual famine year, when the first rain came late, on the first of ניסן.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: Thus said Rabbi Yochanan:
In the days of Yoel son of Pethuel
this verse was fulfilled,
about whom it is written:
'What the gazam left, the arbeh ate,' etc.
phrases.notes: יואל א:ד, describing locust plagues that left nothing.

phrases.english: That year, Adar ended
and no rain had fallen;
the first rainfall came down for them
on the first of Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּימֵי יוֹאֵל בֶּן פְּתוּאֵל נִתְקַיֵּים מִקְרָא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge by limiting the פסוק to one specific historical year.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to an exceptional historical case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to describe the normal yearly pattern, which would put the יורה in ניסן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes the special year of יואל, when the first rain was delayed to ראש חודש ניסן. The normal pattern remains יורה in מרחשון.

steps.title: The prophet tells the starving people to sow their last seeds
steps.stepSummary: After the first rain on the first of ניסן, a נביא tells the people to plant. They ask whether they should eat their last bit of grain or plant it and starve. He says to plant anyway, and a miracle reveals hidden grain in the walls and in ant holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prophet said to Israel: Go out and sow! They said to him: Someone who has one קב of wheat or two קבין of barley, should he eat it and live, or plant it and die? He said to them: Even so, go out and sow. A miracle happened for them. They found grain that was hidden in the walls and in ant holes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story of the special drought year from step 8. Here the people are told to plant even though they have almost nothing left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people's question makes sense. Planting their last food during a drought looks like choosing death over life. The נביא insists they plant anyway, and ה׳ rewards their trust with a miracle: extra seed appears from hidden places.

keyTerms.meaning: A small measure of volume, a small amount of food
Should he eat it and live
Ant holes, where ants store grain

phrases.english: The prophet said to Israel:
Go out and sow!
They said to him: One who has
one kav of wheat or two kav of barley,
phrases.notes: Barley is cheaper, so a person might have twice as much of it.

phrases.english: should he eat it and live,
or sow it and die?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן
phrases.english: He said to them: Even so,
go out and sow.
A miracle was done for them,
and what was in the walls was revealed to them,
and what was in the ant holes.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תירוץ (continuation of the narrative answer begun in step 8)
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם נָבִיא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: צְאוּ וְזִרְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the drought year that רבי יצחק told in step 8 to answer רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people planted their last seed on the word of the נביא, and a miracle gave them hidden grain to plant.

steps.title: The grain grows in eleven days, in time for the עומר
steps.stepSummary: They sowed on the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th of ניסן, and a second rain fell on the 5th. They brought the עומר on the 16th of ניסן. Grain that normally takes six months grew in eleven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went out and sowed on the second, third, and fourth of ניסן. A second rain fell for them on the fifth of ניסן. They brought the עומר on the sixteenth of ניסן. So grain that usually grows in six months grew in eleven days. So the עומר, which is usually brought from grain of six months, was brought from grain of eleven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its high point. The crops grow miraculously fast, so the עומר offering is brought at its normal time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows exactly why the פסוק in יואל could call a ניסן rain the ״יורה״: that year the first rain really did come in ניסן. The eleven days run from the 5th of ניסן (the second rain) to the 16th (the עומר). That is the length of time the grain grew.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: The 'eleven days' count from the second rain on the 5th of ניסן to the 16th of ניסן. They do not count from the planting days.
steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the answer to רב נחמן. Rain in ניסן can be called the first rain, the יורה, in this unusual year, so רבי מאיר's פסוק stands.

phrases.english: They went out and sowed on the second, third, and fourth (of Nisan),
and the second rainfall came down for them
on the fifth of Nisan.
They offered the omer on the sixteenth of Nisan.
It turns out that grain which grows in six months
grew in eleven days.
It turns out that the omer, which is offered
from grain of six months,

phrases.aramaic: קָרֵב מִתְּבוּאָה שֶׁל אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם.
phrases.english: was offered from grain of eleven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְאוּ וְזָרְעוּ שֵׁנִי וּשְׁלִישִׁי וּרְבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after they plant, the miracle of fast growth follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: That year the grain grew in eleven days, and the עומר was brought on time.

steps.title: A verse in תהלים describes that generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the פסוק ״הזורעים בדמעה ברנה יקצורו״ to the generation of the drought year. They planted in tears and harvested with joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about that generation the verse says: 'Those who sow in tears will reap with joy. Though he goes along weeping, carrying the bag of seed...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק in תהלים and says it was written about this very generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story fits the פסוק perfectly. The people planted their last seed in fear and tears, and then harvested a miracle crop with joy. This also sets up the next questions about specific words in the פסוק.

phrases.english: And about that generation it says:
'Those who sow in tears will reap with joyful song.
Though he goes along weeping,
carrying the bag of seed, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל אוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the story just told to a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.raayaObject: That the drought-year generation sowed in tears and reaped with joy.

steps.title: What does 'going along weeping' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase ״הלוך ילך ובכה נשא משך״ means in this context.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'Though he goes along weeping, carrying the bag...'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what one specific phrase of the פסוק means. This sets up רבי יהודה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק (sowing in tears, reaping in joy) is clear from the story. But who is the one 'going along weeping'? And how does the weeping turn into joy? The גמרא wants a concrete picture.

phrases.english: What is 'Though he goes along weeping,
carrying the bag, etc.'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״הָלוֹךְ יֵלֵךְ וּבָכֹה נֹשֵׂא מֶשֶׁךְ וְגוֹ׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on one phrase of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The concrete meaning of ״הלוך ילך ובכה... בא יבא ברנה״ in light of the miracle year.

steps.title: The weeping ox eats fresh sprouts on its way back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that the ox wept as it plowed. On its way back down the same furrow, it could already eat young sprouts, because the grain grew so fast. That is the meaning of ״בא יבא ברנה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: The ox, while plowing, would go along weeping. But on its way back, it would eat fresh young sprouts from the furrow. And this is the meaning of 'He will surely come back with joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question. The 'one who goes weeping' is the plowing ox, and its 'joyful return' is eating sprouts that had already grown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture shows how fast the miracle was. The seed sprouted in the time it took the ox to plow one row and turn back. So the same furrow that brought weeping on the way out brought food and joy on the way back.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
The ox, when it plows,
goes along weeping,
and on its return, it eats young sprouts from the furrow.
And this is: 'He will surely come back with joy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: שׁוֹר, כְּשֶׁהוּא חוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The weeping one is the plowing ox. Its joyful return is eating sprouts that grew instantly in the furrow it had just plowed.

steps.title: What does 'carrying his sheaves' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק, ״נשא אלומותיו״, tells us about that year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'carrying his sheaves'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another phrase in the same פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what was special about the sheaves of that year. Why does the פסוק stress carrying them?

phrases.english: What is 'carrying his sheaves'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״נֹשֵׂא אֲלֻמֹּתָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the middle of the פסוק to its final phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was unusual about the sheaves of the miracle year.

steps.title: The stalk was one span and the ear was two spans
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (and some say a ברייתא) explains that the stalk was only one זרת long, but the ear of grain was two זרתות. The ears were huge compared to the stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: The stalk was one span, and the ear of grain was two spans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The sheaves of that year were special because the grain-bearing ears were twice as long as their stalks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the stalk is much longer than the ear. That year it was the reverse, so most of the plant was edible grain. This is the 'joy' of carrying the sheaves: an unusually rich harvest.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (another version of who said it)
A ברייתא (teaching from the time of the תנאים)
A span (thumb to pinky, hand spread out)

steps.whatToRemember: The drought year of יואל ended with a miracle. The grain grew in eleven days, the עומר came on time, oxen ate sprouts on the return trip down the furrow, and the ears were twice as long as their stalks. That year the first rain, the יורה, came in ניסן. This is how רבי מאיר's פסוק is explained.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
The stalk was a span,
the ear was two spans.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sheaves were special because each ear of grain was two spans long on a stalk of only one span.

steps.title: What did they eat during the seven years of famine?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק what people ate during the seven-year famine mentioned in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'For ה׳ has called for a famine, and it will also come upon the land for seven years'? In those seven years, what did they eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new series of questions from רב נחמן to רבי יצחק. The first one asks how people survived a famine that lasted seven whole years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven years is a very long time to go without food. רב נחמן wants to know how the people stayed alive for that long. This sets up רבי יוחנן's year-by-year answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For ה׳ has called for a famine

phrases.aramaic: וְגַם בָּא אֶל הָאָרֶץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים״,
phrases.english: and it will also come upon the land for seven years",
In those seven years, what did they eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the discussion of drought and hunger in the earlier steps and opens a new series of פסוק questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How people survived during the seven years of famine.

steps.title: Year by year: what they ate during the famine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן with a year-by-year list. Each year the food got worse, until in the seventh year they ate their own arms.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said. In the first year they ate what was stored in their houses. In the second, what was in their fields. In the third, the meat of kosher animals. In the fourth, the meat of non-kosher animals. In the fifth, the meat of insects and creeping creatures. In the sixth, the flesh of their sons and daughters. In the seventh, the flesh of their own arms. This fulfilled the פסוק 'Each man will eat the flesh of his own arm.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers with a list from רבי יוחנן showing how the people sank lower each year of the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each year they used up one kind of food and had to turn to something worse. The list goes from stored food, to permitted meat, to forbidden meat, to the most horrible things of all. The last year matches the פסוק in ישעיה exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Disgusting creatures and creeping things, such as insects

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
In the first year they ate what was in the houses,
in the second they ate what was in the fields,
in the third, the meat of kosher animals,
in the fourth, the meat of non-kosher animals,
in the fifth, the meat of disgusting and creeping creatures,
in the sixth, the flesh of their sons and daughters,
in the seventh, the flesh of their own arms,
to fulfill what is stated:
"Each man shall eat the flesh of his own arm."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each year they ate something worse, ending with their own arms in the seventh year, as the פסוק in ישעיה describes.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן

steps.title: What does 'Holy in your midst, and I will not enter the city' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק about a פסוק in הושע that seems to make no sense: because there is holiness in your midst, ה׳ will not come into the city?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'Holy in your midst, and I will not enter the city'? Because there is holiness in your midst, ה׳ will not enter the city?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks a second question about a confusing פסוק. He points out that its plain reading seems backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You would expect holiness among the people to be a reason for ה׳ to come into the city, not a reason to stay away. רב נחמן spells out this difficulty so that רבי יצחק will explain what the פסוק really means.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not enter the city

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Holy in your midst, and I will not enter the city"?
Because there is holiness in your midst,
I will not enter the city?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, unrelated question in the same series from רב נחמן to רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to make sense of a פסוק that seems to say holiness keeps ה׳ away from the city.

steps.title: ה׳ will not enter the heavenly ירושלים before the earthly one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן: הקדוש ברוך הוא said He will not enter ירושלים של מעלה until He enters ירושלים של מטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said. הקדוש ברוך הוא said: I will not enter the ירושלים above until I enter the ירושלים below.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that 'the city' in the פסוק refers to the heavenly ירושלים. ה׳ will not enter it until the earthly ירושלים is holy and rebuilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two parts of the פסוק are read together. Only when there is holiness 'in your midst,' meaning in the earthly ירושלים, will ה׳ enter the heavenly city. So the difficulty in Step 18 disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mean ה׳ is staying away from holiness. 'The city' He will not enter is the heavenly ירושלים, and He is waiting until the earthly one is ready.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I will not enter the Jerusalem above
until I enter the Jerusalem below!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The city' is the heavenly ירושלים, which ה׳ will not enter until He enters the earthly ירושלים.

steps.title: Is there really a ירושלים above?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a heavenly ירושלים actually exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there such a thing as a ירושלים above?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the idea that the last answer depends on. Is there really a ירושלים in heaven?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's explanation works only if a heavenly ירושלים exists. The גמרא wants a source for that idea before accepting the answer.

phrases.english: And is there a Jerusalem above?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the idea that the answer in Step 19 relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a heavenly ירושלים exists.

steps.title: Proof from תהלים that there is a ירושלים above
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, quoting 'ירושלים built as a city that is joined together.' This hints that there are two cities of ירושלים, joined to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it is written: 'ירושלים that is built like a city that is joined together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a פסוק from תהלים as its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'joined together' suggest that ירושלים is connected to something that matches it. That match is the heavenly ירושלים. So the two cities exist and are tied together, which supports רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a heavenly ירושלים tied to the earthly one. ה׳ will not enter the heavenly city until the earthly ירושלים is restored.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the heavenly world to what happens on earth. Rebuilding the earthly ירושלים matters even 'above.'

phrases.english: Yes, as it is written:
"Jerusalem that is built
like a city that is joined together."
phrases.notes: 'Joined together' hints at two cities of Jerusalem, one above and one below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 20 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The פסוק 'a city that is joined together' shows that the earthly ירושלים is joined to a heavenly one.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks about 'and with one they are brutish'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רבי יצחק what the פסוק in ירמיה means: 'And with one they are brutish and foolish, the teaching of vanities is wood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: What does the פסוק mean, 'And with one they are brutish and foolish, the teaching of vanities is wood'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a new puzzling פסוק to רבי יצחק, just as he did with the earlier questions. He wants to know what the 'one' thing is that makes people foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'with one,' but it never says one what. That missing word is the puzzle. The word יבערו can also hint at 'burning' (from בער), and the answer will use that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
They are brutish; this also hints at 'burning'
Wood; here, a block of wood, meaning an idol

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And with one they are brutish and foolish,
the teaching of vanities is wood"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new question in the same series of רב נחמן's questions to רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the unnamed 'one' thing in the פסוק that makes people brutish and foolish?

steps.title: The 'one' is idol worship, which burns the wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק answers in the name of רבי יוחנן: the 'one' is a single sin that burns the wicked in גיהנם, and that sin is עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said. There is one sin that burns the wicked in גיהנם. What is it? עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק fills in the missing word. The 'one' is one sin, עבודה זרה, which brings the wicked to burn in גיהנם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads יבערו as 'they burn' instead of only 'they are brutish.' That turns the פסוק into a statement about punishment: one sin burns people in גיהנם. He then names that sin as עבודה זרה, and the next step proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment after death

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is one thing that burns
the wicked in Gehinnom.
What is it? Idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'one' is the sin of עבודה זרה, which burns the wicked in גיהנם.

steps.title: Proof from the shared word הבל
steps.stepSummary: The proof that the פסוק is about עבודה זרה: the word הבל appears here and also in a later פסוק that clearly describes idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here, 'the teaching of vanities (הבלים) is wood,' and it is written there, 'they are vanity (הבל), a work of delusion.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves that the 'one' sin is עבודה זרה. The same word, הבל, shows up in another פסוק that is clearly talking about idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a word link (similar to a גזירה שוה). Later in the same chapter of ירמיה, idols are called 'הבל, a work of delusion.' So when our פסוק says 'מוסר הבלים,' it is also talking about idols.

phrases.english: It is written here:
"The teaching of vanities is wood,"
and it is written there:
"They are vanity, a work of delusion."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This proves the claim in step 23 that the 'one' sin is עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the 'one' sin in the פסוק is עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word הבל, which ירמיה י:טו uses to describe idols.
steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, 'with one they burn' means one sin, עבודה זרה, which sends the wicked to burn in גיהנם. The word הבל connects the two פסוקים.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks why the verse counts only two evils
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks about 'For my people have committed two evils.' Were there only two? What about the twenty-four sins listed by יחזקאל? Were those just let go?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said to רבי יצחק: What does the פסוק mean, 'For My people have committed two evils'? Were there only two? Were the twenty-four other sins just left aside?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks a new question about a פסוק in ירמיה. It counts only two evils, but other נביאים list many more sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the number. יחזקאל lists twenty-four sins of the people, so saying 'two evils' looks like the other twenty-four were forgiven or ignored. That cannot be right, so רב נחמן wants to know what 'two' really means.

keyTerms.meaning: Were left aside for them, meaning let go or forgiven

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the people only did two sins. He is asking how the פסוק can say 'two' when we know there were many more.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"For My people have committed two evils"?
Were there only two?
Were the twenty-four left aside for them?
phrases.notes: The twenty-four sins listed in יחזקאל

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new question in the same series. It is again about ירמיה and again about counting sins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק say only 'two evils' when יחזקאל lists twenty-four sins?

steps.title: רבי יצחק begins answering in רבי יוחנן's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק begins to answer in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'There is one sin that is...' The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said. There is one sin that is...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק starts his answer to the 'two evils' question. This passage cuts off mid-sentence, and the rest of the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer opens with 'one sin that is,' just like the previous answer did. The sentence finishes on the next amud: there is one sin, עבודה זרה, that is equal to two. So the 'two evils' in the פסוק describe one sin, and it is counted as two.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is one sin that is...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַחַת שֶׁהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins the answer to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer has only begun. It points to one sin that counts as two (completed on the next amud as עבודה זרה).
